literal: For virtue those who are worthy who if you ask, in the dread-water world, to others she who belongs shoulders those who do not touch.
translation: If you ask, 'Who are those worthy of virtue in this world surrounded by the dread ocean?' They are those who do not embrace the shoulders of a woman who belongs to another.
modern: அச்சம் தரும் கடல் சூழ்ந்த இவ்வுலகத்தில், அறத்திற்கு உரியவர் யார் என்று கேட்டால், அவர் பிறனுக்கு உரியவளின் தோள்களைத் தீண்டாதவர் ஆவார்.
explanation: This couplet defines the ultimate standard of virtue in the world. The poet uses the phrase 'நாமநீர் வைப்பு' (the world surrounded by the terrifying, vast ocean) to establish a grand, global scale. Within this vast world, the highest moral excellence is attributed to those who possess the self-control to never embrace another man's wife ('பிறர்க்குரியாள் தோள்தோயாதார்'). Their restraint is marked as the defining qualification for true goodness.
